title: ADVISORY VOTE: Should Troutdale Create a Municipal Police Department?
ballot_label: Caption: ADVISORY VOTE: Should Troutdale Create a Municipal Police Department? Question: ADVISORY VOTE: Should the City proceed with planning and creation of a Troutdale Police Department?
summary: A non-binding advisory question. Troutdale dissolved its police department in 2015 and contracts with the Multnomah County Sheriff's Office; contract costs have since risen. The vote asks whether the City should continue planning a municipal police department. It does not authorize creating one, any tax, fee or expenditure, hiring, or ending the contract.
yes_means: A yes vote advises the City that voters support proceeding with planning and creation of a Troutdale Police Department; the vote is non-binding.
no_means: A no vote advises the City that voters do not support proceeding with planning and creation of a Troutdale Police Department; the vote is non-binding.
fiscal_impact: None directly: the ballot summary states the advisory vote does not authorize or impose any tax, fee, or expenditure. The City's preliminary analysis projects a municipal department at a cost comparable to, and potentially less than, continued contracted services.

arguments.author: City of Troutdale (explanatory statement, submitted by Sarah Skroch, City Recorder)
arguments.statement: The City's explanatory statement says supporters cite local control over policing priorities, direct accountability to City leadership, and officers assigned only to Troutdale.
arguments.excerpt: Supporters of a municipal Police Department identify potential benefits including local control over policing priorities, direct accountability to City leadership, officers assigned exclusively to the City of Troutdale,

arguments.author: City of Troutdale (explanatory statement, submitted by Sarah Skroch, City Recorder)
arguments.statement: The explanatory statement says supporters note a locally managed department may make future police service costs more predictable.
arguments.excerpt: Supporters also note that a locally managed department may provide greater predictability in future police service costs

arguments.author: Josh Smith, Troutdale resident
arguments.statement: In a 2026 KATU report, Troutdale resident Josh Smith said that with a local department, residents learn to trust officers and the community.
arguments.excerpt: Locals learn to trust in officers, in the community, in the people, in the high schools.

arguments.author: David Hill, Troutdale resident
arguments.statement: In a 2026 KATU report, resident David Hill said he has always supported Troutdale having its own police department, as it did in the past.
arguments.excerpt: I always support Troutdale having its own police department as they had their own police department in the past.

arguments.author: City of Troutdale (explanatory statement, submitted by Sarah Skroch, City Recorder)
arguments.statement: The explanatory statement says those favoring the current contract note it provides access to regional investigative resources, specialized units and a larger law enforcement network.
arguments.excerpt: They note that the current model provides access to regional investigative resources, specialized units, emergency response capabilities, established administrative systems, and a larger regional law enforcement network.

arguments.author: City of Troutdale (explanatory statement, submitted by Sarah Skroch, City Recorder)
arguments.statement: The explanatory statement says contract supporters point to the costs and challenges of starting a new department, including recruiting staff, buying equipment, and writing policies.
arguments.excerpt: They also point to the costs and operational challenges associated with establishing a new Police Department, including recruiting and retaining qualified personnel, purchasing equipment, developing policies and procedures,

arguments.author: Sgt. Joshua Zwick, Multnomah County Sheriff's Office; president, Deputy Sheriff's Association
arguments.statement: In a 2026 KATU report, Sheriff's Office Sgt. Joshua Zwick said Troutdale's proposed policing model is far less than what the city has now.
arguments.excerpt: the policing model that Troutdale's put forward is far less than what they have now

arguments.author: Sgt. Joshua Zwick, Multnomah County Sheriff's Office; president, Deputy Sheriff's Association
arguments.statement: Zwick said the proposed model would not provide 24/7 coverage to Troutdale residents.
arguments.excerpt: it won't cover 24/7 to the citizens of Troutdale, which is a huge problem.

gaps: Official voters' pamphlet arguments (yes and no) could not be read: the county pamphlet PDF text is truncated before the measures section.
collection_notes: Voters' pamphlet: the SOS Book 13 PDF text (120,052 chars) ends at the statewide section; the multco.us English (104,260 chars) and large-print (105,643 chars) county pamphlet PDFs are cut off by WebFetch text extraction in the candidate statements, before the Measures & Arguments section, so printed pamphlet arguments (if any) could not be read. The SOS Spanish-language Multnomah guide (ES-MUL-1126) was checked only to see whether arguments exist: per the fetch tool it prints the measure and an explanation for each of 26-265 to 26-269 but no argument sections; translated guides may omit arguments, so this is not conclusive. The Sept 8, 2026 argument deadline has passed per the county filings page. Measure document PDFs on multco.us (measure_26-26x/download, referral documents) have no machine-readable text (scanned). WebFetch limits quotes to 125 characters, so several excerpts are sentence segments. yes_means/no_means are not official text: Oregon local ballot titles have no official result-of-vote statement, so they are neutral one-sentence descriptions written strictly from the official ballot question. Inventory title, number and jurisdiction match the multco.us page and filings list (filed 8/12/2026). The explanatory statement itself presents both supporters' and contract-supporters' views; those are recorded as kind 'explainer' (2 yes, 2 no). KATU quotes (July 14, 2026) predate the Aug 12 measure filing and concern the City's proposal to revive the department, which this advisory vote asks about. Zwick is an MCSO sergeant and union president (the current contractor's employee association). Balanced 4 yes / 4 no.
